transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (EdgePay CTO), Priya Singh (EdgePay Lead ML Eng), Noah Miller (EdgePay Product)

Summary:
- Weekly POC sync for caching work (prefix + KV cache). Review of current hit-rates, tuning experiments, and next steps for a 24h benchmark run. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Current KV and prefix cache hit rates and distribution
- Prompt reuse / canonicalization strategy
- Cache key composition and privacy concerns
- TTLs and eviction policy tuning
- Benchmark plan and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Liam, Priya, Noah from EdgePay and Miguel and myself from Redwood. We have 45 minutes, main goal is to review the caching numbers from this week and agree next steps.
[00:22] Liam: Yep, here.
[00:24] Priya: Present.
[00:26] Noah: Here.
[00:30] Miguel: Hey team.
[00:33] Ava: Cool. Miguel, do you want to kick off with the hit-rate summary?
[00:38] Miguel: Sure. So quick recap, we ran the updated prefix caching logic on Tuesday for a 6h window with production-ish traffic. High level: overall KV (or K V in some logs) cache hit-rate was about 42% for the last test, prefix-only reuse was around 35% when we count re-used prompt prefixes. We also saw that about 18% of hits are from exact-template matches, whereas the rest are param-normalized matches.
[01:12] Priya: When you say param-normalized, do you mean you canonicalize numeric slots or you hash the serialized params?
[01:18] Miguel: Good question. Right now we do a lightweight canonicalization: strip whitespace, normalize date formats to iso, and collapse numeric tokens to a placeholder token for matching. We then compute key = sha256(system_prompt + template_hash + param_signature). That param_signature is intentionally lossy to increase reuse.
[01:36] Priya: Hm that's helpful. Any idea how much of the miss-rate is because of user-specific metadata in prompts? We have lots of prompts that include account ids, user names, etc.
[01:46] Miguel: Yes, we profiled that — approx 22% of unique keys are attributable to user-specific tokens. Those should be high-value to strip or replace with stable placeholders to boost reuse.
[01:55] Noah: Are we comfortable with removing those fields from cache keys given EdgePay's audit & compliance?
[02:01] Ava: We flagged privacy earlier — we won't store raw PII in the cached payload. Redwood supports redaction hooks and you can opt to hash user ids before they become part of keys. Also we can keep per-customer cache partitions in Dedicated/Private so you get isolation.
[02:18] Liam: Good. What's the latency impact we're seeing? Because even if hit-rate increases, we need tail latency improvements if possible.
[02:25] Miguel: Right now median token latency for a hit path is ~120ms, miss path median is ~240ms. P99 overall with current batching is ~420ms. If we push hit rate to the 65-75% range, our estimate based on traces is p99 ~300-320ms. That's using the current model variant and no quantization changes.
[02:50] Priya: That p99 delta is meaningful. What's blocking us from hitting 65%? Is it TTLs, key strategy, or prompt variation?
[02:58] Miguel: A mix. Short TTLs on some high churn templates (we used 1h TTL for user-facing confirmations) plus too many slightly different templates. We also observed that templated questions with appended freeform user input kill prefix reuse.
[03:12] Priya: For the freeform bits, is there a threshold where we stop caching beyond a token length or character pattern?
[03:20] Miguel: We have a rule currently: if the variable segment is longer than 64 tokens or contains punctuation that looks like long-form text, we avoid caching. We can tune that.
[03:28] Noah: Another ask — could we have a reduced-response cache: cache the generated tokens up to the first 50 tokens and then generate rest live? Might help if many responses start with same boilerplate.
[03:40] Miguel: Interesting idea. We have partial-prefix caching already conceptually, but not deployed. We can prototype caching the first N tokens of the model response as a prefix. Need to evaluate memory cost.
[03:50] Ava: Ok let's park that as a design spike. Miguel, add to action items.
[03:55] Miguel: Noted.
[03:58] [04:00] Miguel: Back to hit-rate distribution — the top 20 templates account for ~56% of cacheable calls. That means if EdgePay shares those templates we can prioritize key normalization rules for big wins.
[04:15] Priya: We'll prepare the top templates. We'll also flag which contain PII and which require residency constraints.
[04:22] Ava: Great. On TTLs — we experimented with 1h vs 6h vs 24h. In the 6h run, hit-rate bumped from 42% to 53% but we saw slightly stale outputs on a small percentage of confirmations. For most prompts, 24h looks fine but confirmations/transactional messages need shorter TTLs.
[04:45] Liam: Could we do tag-based TTLs? e.g., transactional:true => 1h, informational => 24h.
[04:51] Miguel: Yes, we support tag-based TTLs, and can automate based on template metadata. That would allow us to keep safety for transactional templates while benefiting other templates.
[04:59] Priya: What's the storage/memory impact of increasing TTLs globally?
[05:04] Miguel: With current traffic, increasing to 24h would grow the cache working set by ~2.6x. For the Dedicated pool we're using, that is within capacity but increases eviction churn slightly. We'll include memory delta in the 24h bench report.
[05:18] Noah: How are you measuring hits? Are these application-level cache hits or runtime token-level hits?
[05:24] Miguel: We report both. The metrics we shared are request-level hits for prefix and KV. We also surface token-level savings. In this rollout we reduced total output tokens by ~17% during the 6h run.
[05:36] Priya: 17% token reduction is already decent. Our internal cost model says 15% reduces spend by about 12% net after latency/bandwidth.
[05:45] Ava: That aligns. Success criteria that we discussed earlier was 20% token reduction or 70% request-level cache hit-rate depending on approach. We should pick one for the 24h run as primary.
[05:56] Liam: Let's aim for token reduction for cost-first: target 20% token reduction, secondary target p99 latency under 350ms.
[06:03] Ava: Sounds good. Miguel, can you run the 24h bench with TTLs tuned and the canonicalization rules and report token reduction and p99?
[06:09] Miguel: Yup. I'll run two variants: conservative canonicalization (strip whitespace, normalize dates) and aggressive (strip user ids and collapse numeric tokens). We'll also include a run with prefix-first-50-token caching prototype.
[06:20] Priya: For the aggressive canonicalization, we need to see exact transformations so we can validate outputs for compliance. We'll need diffs and examples.
[06:28] Miguel: Understood. We'll include a sample diff set highlighting changed outputs and the templates that got canonicalized.
[06:33] Ava: Also we'll share the dashboard link and the CSV of hit-rate time series so you can slice by template and user segment.
[06:40] Priya: Good. Please scrub any raw PII before sharing.
[06:43] Ava: We'll hash any raw ids, and mark the ones that were redacted in the CSV.
[06:49] Noah: Quick question on key composition: you mentioned system_prompt + template_hash + param_signature. Can we add a tenant_id prefix so EdgePay can later evict per-customer keys?
[06:59] Miguel: Yes, tenant_id is already first-class in the key; apologies if that wasn't explicit in the doc. So cache partitions are per-tenant by default.
[07:07] Priya: For the canonicalization rules, can we have them configured per-template? Some templates are sensitive and can't lose tokens.
[07:13] Miguel: Absolutely — rules can be attached at template metadata level. We'll show the UI for that in the follow-up.
[07:19] Liam: Any risks with caching layered responses that include account balances or ephemeral tokens?
[07:24] Ava: We flagged ephemeral tokens earlier — we won't cache responses that include the ephemeral token pattern. We can also detect time-limited values via regex.
[07:32] Miguel: One more note from the logs: we saw a pathological template that mutated slightly per request due to a non-deterministic timestamp formatting in your microservice. That killed reuse; you might want to normalize at the SDK side.
[07:44] Priya: That's on us — we'll push a change to the SDK to emit iso timestamps.
[07:49] Ava: Nice. Ok let's cover the experimental results details Miguel prepared.
[07:53] Miguel: In the slides (referenced in the shared doc) — the conservative run: TTL 6h, canonicalization basic => request hit-rate 53%, token reduction 17%, p99 360ms. Aggressive run: TTL 24h + param collapse => hit-rate 68%, token reduction 24%, p99 290ms. The prefix-first-50 prototype improved median but had bigger memory footprint and some slight divergence in rare templates.
[08:24] Noah: That aggressive run looks promising. What's the divergence you saw?
[08:28] Miguel: On about 0.4% of calls, the canonicalization removed tokens that were used in downstream business logic - e.g., order reference numbers that later get looked up. For those templates we need a whitelist to avoid canonicalizing.
[08:44] Priya: We'll share that list.
[08:46] Ava: Great. On rollout strategy: propose we can canary the aggressive canonicalization on 10% of traffic for 72h, monitor correctness metrics and cost, then expand. Thoughts?
[08:57] Liam: Works for us as long as we get diffs and watch the business logic errors.
[09:03] Miguel: We'll instrument a correctness metric that flags mismatches against a golden path for a sample set.
[09:09] Priya: How about SLOs during canary? We want no more than 0.1% correctness regression and p99 under 350ms.
[09:16] Ava: We'll set alerts for that.
[09:18] Miguel: Also note: we need to tune eviction policy to prefer LRU with weighted size because some cached values are big. That reduces churn.
[09:28] Noah: Ok. For next steps, timeline?
[09:31] Ava: Miguel will run 24h bench and share CSV + dashboard by 2025-03-05. EdgePay will share top template taxonomy and PII flags by 2025-03-06. Then we run a canary starting 2025-03-09 for 72h and meet 2025-03-11 to review.
[09:47] Priya: Confirming those dates.
[09:50] Liam: Confirmed.
[09:52] Ava: Anything else?
[09:54] Noah: One small ask — can Redwood provide a simple runbook for how to opt templates in/out of caching? Our product folks want the UI steps.
[10:02] Miguel: We'll draft runbook and include UI screenshots, and config API calls.
[10:07] Ava: Great. We'll attach that to the follow-up email.
[10:10] Priya: Thanks everyone, this was productive.
[10:13] Ava: Thanks all. Quick recap of action items in chat and we'll share the links.
[10:18] Miguel: End of notes.
